elements.quote: Background: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the current limited evidence base for evaluating sustainability of EBIs, describing the knowledge gap and uncertainty motivating the review.

elements.quote: As evaluation is necessary to determine effectiveness, this review aimed to improve our understanding of how the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare is evaluated.
elements.reason: The authors state the purpose and importance of the review—improving understanding of sustainability evaluation—explaining the need for conducting the review.

elements.quote: A focus on evaluation is what differentiates this review from recent syntheses published on approaches to sustainability research.
elements.reason: The manuscript compares the current review to existing syntheses and explains how and why this review is needed in relation to prior work (distinguishing scope).

The review focuses on approaches to evaluate sustainability of EBIs rather than on reviewing intervention effects; thus describing a proposed mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.
The review synthesizes evaluation approaches for sustainability rather than evaluating a specific complex intervention or its delivery context, so inclusion of a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare. We aimed to enhance our understanding of sustainability definitions, research designs, data collection methods, timing, measures, and sustainability outcomes used for sustainability evaluation studies.
elements.reason: The review's objectives are explicitly stated (to identify and synthesize approaches and to enhance understanding of specific elements), but they are not presented using a formal question‑formulation framework (e.g., PICO, PCC) as required by the element.

elements.quote: We conducted an integrative review that followed Whittemore and Knafl's [12] five-stage methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis (data reduction, display, comparison, and conclusions); and (5) presentation. Integrative reviews can include diverse data sources and do not restrict the type of study design. Furthermore, integrative reviews take a more flexible approach to analysis compared to systematic reviews, combining both quantitative and qualitative data if there are similarities [12-14].
elements.reason: This review is an integrative review of evaluation approaches rather than a review of intervention effects; therefore specifying planned comparisons using PICO (or variant) is not applicable.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal • Were primary research • Had explicit research design and data collection methods • Had an explicit theoretical ­ approach a for sustainability ­ (theory b , ­ model c , ­ framework d , ­ instrument e , method, checklist, process, strategy, conceptual- izations, development, pilot test and/or ­ tool f ) • Were within a healthcare ­ setting g • Evaluated the sustainability of an EBI (Note that inconsistent terminology for EBI is prominent and thus may be referred to as a QI intervention/ initia- tive in the literature).
elements.reason: Table 1 explicitly lists study characteristics used for eligibility including study design (primary research), required explicit research design and data collection, required theoretical approach, healthcare setting, and that the study evaluated sustainability of an EBI.

elements.quote: We only included published studies in the English language and peer-reviewed primary studies in this review.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies language (English) and publication/report status (published, peer-reviewed primary studies) but does not specify or provide eligibility criteria regarding dissemination year or other report-characteristic restrictions (no year limits reported).
No explicit distinction is reported between excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus excluding because outcome results were not reported.
The report does not specify groups used in each synthesis nor link groups to comparisons defined in the review objectives.
No rationale is provided for notable restrictions on study eligibility (e.g., exclusion of gray literature or English-only restriction is stated but not justified in the methods as a rationale).

elements.quote: In December 2018 and July 2020, we searched the following databases: Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process and Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly reports the dates on which the database searches were conducted (December 2018 and July 2020).

elements.quote: we searched the following databases: Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process and Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current).
elements.reason: The manuscript lists each bibliographic database by name, provides the platform/interface (e.g., Ovid MEDLINE, OVID Embase, EBSCOhost CINAHL, Wiley Cochrane Library) and reports available coverage dates for each.

elements.quote: Additional file 1. Search strategy. The four databases searched on Dec 21, 2018, as well as an additional search in July 2020. The file depicts the date of searchers and strategy used, including all search terms in each database.
elements.reason: The supplementary material (Additional file 1) is explicitly stated to contain the full search strategy, dates, and all search terms for each database, indicating the complete search strategies are reported (in the supplement).

elements.quote: We only included published studies in the English language and peer-reviewed primary studies in this review. This review entailed a comprehensive search of published literature and rigorous review methods; however, we recognize that there is the possibility of incomplete retrieval of identified research. For example, all gray literature was excluded.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes specific search limits (English language, peer-reviewed only, exclusion of gray literature) but does not provide a clear justification tied to the eligibility criteria beyond stating the inclusion scope; thus limits are described but not fully justified by reference to eligibility criteria.
No evidence was found that published search approaches or filters were cited nor that adaptations to such filters were described in the provided text.

elements.quote: In the first screening stage, one reviewer (RF) independently screened the abstracts and titles of all the citations retrieved from the database searches. A second reviewer (AB) independently screened a randomly selected 10% of all titles and abstracts to verify selection for inclusion or exclusion. In the second stage, two reviewers (RF and AB) independently screened all full-text articles that had passed first-stage screening.
elements.reason: The text explicitly reports the number of reviewers at each stage: one primary reviewer screened all titles/abstracts, a second reviewer screened 10% for verification, and two reviewers independently screened all full texts.

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite), (3) sustainability definition and terms used, (4) type and name of theoretical approach, (5) purpose of approach use, (6) data collection methods, (7) timing of evaluation data collection (e.g., pre-, and/or post-implementation of intervention), (8) reported sustainability measures and, 9. reported sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: Explicitly states that two reviewers extracted data from reports.

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite), (3) sustainability definition and terms used, (4) type and name of theoretical approach, (5) purpose of approach use, (6) data collection methods, (7) timing of evaluation data collection (e.g., pre-, and/or post-implementation of intervention), (8) reported sustainability measures and, 9. reported sustainability outcomes.

No methods reported for translating articles for data collection in the provided evidence.
No specification of software used to extract data from figures is present in the supplied evidence.
No decision rules described for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies between them in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: We extracted whether an included study evaluated (a) sustainability determinants and (b) sustainability outcomes and how they measured these variables. We defined sustainability determinants as correlates and predictors of sustainability (organizational, contextual, and strategies) and sustainability outcomes as the subsequent impact (healthcare improvement or public health outcomes) of sustained intervention use [5]. To further unpack sustainability outcomes, we extracted and synthesized nine sustainability outcomes across the 64 included studies (Table 3) [6, 15, 16].
elements.reason: The manuscript lists and defines the broad outcome domains 'sustainability determinants' and 'sustainability outcomes' and states that nine specific sustainability outcomes were extracted and synthesized (referring to Table 3). However, it does not provide definitions for each of the nine outcome domains in the provided text, so the reporting is partial.

No explicit specification of the time frame of measurement for each outcome domain is provided in the retrieved evidence. Timing of evaluations is reported generally, but not time frames tied to each outcome domain.
The manuscript does not state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (e.g., all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
There is no description of a process used to select results when not all compatible results were sought; the retrieved evidence does not report such a selection process.
No information is provided about changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or their importance or rationales for changes.
No reporting of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains or rationales for such changes is present in the provided evidence.
The manuscript does not report which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions nor provide a rationale for any prioritisation in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite), (3) sustainability definition and terms used, (4) type and name of theoretical approach, (5) purpose of approach use, (6) data collection methods, (7) timing of evaluation data collection (e.g., pre-, and/or post-implementation of intervention), (8) reported sustainability measures and, 9. reported sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the other variables extracted and defines timing with an example; several theoretical approach types are also defined nearby in the same chunk (footnotes a–g).
No text in the provided evidence explicitly describes assumptions made about missing or unclear study information.

The evidence does not cite any tool used to determine which data items to collect; tools mentioned (e.g., MMAT) relate to quality appraisal, not selection of data items, and no explicit citation of a tool for data-item determination is provided.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: The specific risk-of-bias tool (MMAT) is named, but no version number or year of the MMAT is reported in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: The MMAT [17] appraises the quality by study design type, such as quantitative, qualitative, or mixed empirical methods. ... The criteria are specific to each type of study, with five domains apportioned to qualitative studies and quantitative studies subdivided into randomized controlled, non-randomized and descriptive studies.
elements.reason: The evidence specifies that MMAT assesses by study design and mentions five domains for qualitative studies and subdivisions for quantitative studies, but it does not list the specific domains, components, or individual items assessed.

elements.quote: Each study is assigned an overall quality score, using asterisks representing the quality appraisal of each study. Scores vary from 20% (*) when one criterion is met to 100% (*****) when all criteria are met.
elements.reason: An overall risk/quality judgement (an overall score represented by asterisks and percentage) is reported and the rules for deriving the score (mapping number of criteria met to percentage/asterisks) are described.
No information is provided in the retrieved evidence about any adaptations made to the MMAT or other risk-of-bias tools.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool is reported in the evidence; this conditional item does not apply.

elements.quote: Two reviewers independently completed MMAT assessments and compared scoring.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two), that they worked independently, and that they compared scoring (procedure for resolving differences) are explicitly reported.
No processes for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators are described in the provided evidence.
The evidence does not describe use of any automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment (use, training, performance, or validation).

No text in the provided methods or results describes effect measures used for each outcome (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) or specifies effect measures for outcomes; the methods describe study selection, data extraction, and types of data collected but not effect measures.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes or rationale are reported in the provided evidence.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described in the supplied methods or results text.
The provided evidence contains no justification for the choice of any effect measure.

elements.quote: We compared, grouped, and synthesized each study by these variables. Evidence tables were created to summarize and describe the studies included in this review.
elements.reason: The manuscript states that studies were compared, grouped, and synthesized by the extracted variables and that evidence tables were created to summarize studies, which indicates a general process for deciding study inclusion in syntheses. However, it does not provide detailed methods for how studies were allocated to specific syntheses (e.g., exact decision rules, tabulation against planned groups, or criteria applied per synthesis), so the reporting is partial rather than fully descriptive.

The provided evidence does not describe any methods used to prepare data for presentation or synthesis (e.g., handling of missing summary statistics, data transformations or conversions). While data extraction variables and general analysis stages are reported (text_10, text_8), there is no explicit description of procedures for preparing or converting collected data for synthesis.

elements.quote: Evidence tables were created to summarize and describe the studies included in this review.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that evidence tables were created to summarize and describe included studies; Table 4 (table_2) provides an example of such tabular structure (columns for data collection method, counts, and referenced studies) showing the data included in tables.

elements.quote: Figure 1 depicts our search, screening, and selection results using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines flow diagram [18].
elements.reason: The paper reports and includes a PRISMA flow diagram (graphical display of search/screening results), but it does not describe methods for graphical displays more broadly or detail how graphs were generated or formatted.

elements.quote: We compared, grouped, and synthesized each study by these variables. Evidence tables were created to summarize and describe the studies included in this review.
elements.reason: The authors state they compared, grouped and synthesized studies by extracted variables and present evidence tables summarizing studies, which reports the basis for ordering/grouping studies within tables and syntheses.
No text or figure in the provided evidence explains a rationale for using any non-standard graphs or visualizations.
No statistical/meta-analytic synthesis was performed in this integrative review; only EndNote X7 was used as a management system (no software/packages for statistical synthesis reported).

elements.quote: We conducted an integrative review that followed Whittemore and Knafl's [12] five-stage methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis (data reduction, display, comparison, and conclusions); and (5) presentation.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the alternative synthesis approach used (integrative review using Whittemore and Knafl's steps including data reduction, display, comparison, and conclusions) which justifies the non-use of meta-analysis.
No meta-analyses were performed or reported in this integrative review (study describes qualitative/ integrative synthesis methods rather than meta-analysis).
No statistical/meta-analytic methods were reported because no meta-analysis was conducted.
No methods to identify or quantify statistical heterogeneity are reported; no meta-analysis was conducted.
No random-effects meta-analysis was performed, so no between-study variance estimator is reported.
No meta-analysis was undertaken; therefore no method for calculating confidence intervals for a summary effect is reported.
No random-effects implementation details are provided because no random-effects meta-analysis was performed.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed; no priors are described.
No statistical syntheses were performed that would require methods to account for multiple estimates per study.

elements.quote: Methods: Following Whittemore and Knafl's methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis; and (5) presentation, a comprehensive search strategy was applied across five databases.
elements.reason: The review used an integrative synthesis approach and does not report planned quantitative syntheses that were judged impossible; thus this conditional item does not apply.

The study is an integrative review combining qualitative and quantitative data and describes data analysis using Whittemore and Knafl's integrative review steps (data reduction, display, comparison, conclusions) (text_8, text_12). No methods to explore heterogeneity (e.g., subgroup analysis, meta-regression) are described in the Methods or Analysis sections, and no meta-analysis was conducted, so specifying methods to explore statistical heterogeneity does not apply.

No subgroup analyses or meta-regression are reported or described in the Methods or Results (analysis described as integrative, text_8, text_12). Therefore reporting factors, factor levels, and expected direction of effect modification is not applicable.

The review used integrative synthesis methods (Whittemore and Knafl) and did not report quantitative meta-analytic approaches using study-level or within-study contrasts (text_8, text_12). No analyses of that type are described, so this item is not applicable.

Methods to compare subgroup effects are not reported anywhere in the Methods or Results; the review used qualitative/integrative synthesis rather than subgroup comparisons or statistical tests (text_8, text_12), making this item not applicable.

No heterogeneity analyses (pre-specified or post-hoc) are reported in the Methods or Results. The manuscript describes integrative synthesis without statistical heterogeneity analyses (text_8, text_12), so identification of non–pre-specified heterogeneity analyses does not apply.

No text in the provided evidence identifies any sensitivity analyses, pre-specified or not, so none are described as non-pre-specified.
No text in the provided evidence describes any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis or arising from reporting biases.

No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described in the supplied evidence.
There is no description or link to any newly developed reporting-bias tool in the provided evidence.
